### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, touching **5** documentable anchor(s).

**30** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b65488a8a9db73ddbede8a05605137419da28a8e`.

⛔ **11** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **21** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b65488a8a9db73ddbede8a05605137419da28a8e` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `40f28c7de5f4ecb229016570fec4996541a1737c` — the merge of head `13a5b397db366d5a394458464d61b97c80babb08` into base `b65488a8a9db73ddbede8a05605137419da28a8e`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 40f28c7de5f4ecb229016570fec4996541a1737c && git checkout 40f28c7de5f4ecb229016570fec4996541a1737c
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin b65488a8a9db73ddbede8a05605137419da28a8e 13a5b397db366d5a394458464d61b97c80babb08 && git checkout -B drift-repro b65488a8a9db73ddbede8a05605137419da28a8e && git merge --no-ff 13a5b397db366d5a394458464d61b97c80babb08

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b65488a8a9db73ddbede8a05605137419da28a8e
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs b65488a8a9db73ddbede8a05605137419da28a8e` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 维护者速读

- 用户能看到什么变化：通过 AI 助手等入口做分组统计时，如果按"关联对象的字段"分组，现在会立即得到一条说明怎么改的错误，而不是数据库报错或返回一组空值。
- 为什么做：以前三四层关联会报服务器内部错误，一两层报的提示会误导人去同步表结构。
- 出错会怎样：只影响按多层关联路径分组的调用；网页端原本就拒绝这种写法。区域还需确认看板统计的一种写法不受影响。
- 要你做什么：无。区域补齐两项后，交席位复审再落地。

## 席位核对

**L1-a: ACCEPT with two required items before landing** · head `1af59bd01f394549873875423019680a2aa86203` · Fixes #34886 · 2026-11-19T11:43Z

Readings: K=12; `check-governed-merges --pr 35479` not governed; `merge-tree` against main clean; CI 39 success / 18 skipped / 0 failed. The PR is a draft, so mark it ready when R1 and R2 are done.

**Code: sound for the case it targets.** In `assertGroupByTargetsAreStored` (`aggregate-query-shape-door.ts`), an entry whose `field` contains a dot and is not a declared field name is refused `INVALID_FIELD`/400 at `groupBy.N` or `groupBy.N.field`, before the virtual-field check and before any driver runs. A field whose own declared name contains a dot passes through. `REFERENCE_VALUE_TYPES` decides the relation-head hint. `engine-delete-and-aggregate.ts` and driver-sql are untouched. The pins run over real ObjectQL and SqlDriver/SQLite through the MCP bridge: 4, 3 and 1 hops each refused with zero GROUP BY statements, the object form, `aggregateGroups`, and a CONTROL where grouping by the relation field answers in one statement. On main they are 5 failed / 1 passed, and the ablation is red the same way.

**R1 (required): the declaration is a narrowing.** As data-1 asked: an engine that aggregates in memory answered a dotted `groupBy` (one null group, 200), and now refuses it. A published door that used to answer, even wrongly, now refuses. That is the a95cb06 / #35473 reading. Make these changes in the changeset and the PR body:
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`;
- `Metadata-protocol: none` stays, at `patch`;
- a **BREAKING** line saying a dotted `groupBy` reaching `engine.aggregate` past the REST door is now refused, and why it ships `patch`;
- exactly one ADR-0087 marker, in a category that `pnpm check:adr-0087-registration` accepts.

**R2 (required, measure before landing): the analytics own-qualifier path.** `service-analytics`' `ObjectQLStrategy` keeps a dimension spelled behind the cube's own qualifier (`<cube>.<field>`) as base, not cross-object (`isCrossObjectField`, `objectql-strategy.ts:1391-1398`). `declaredCubeMemberKey` (`cube-member-key.ts:61-72`) strips that qualifier only when `<field>` is a declared cube member. Otherwise `lookupCubeMember` returns the dotted spelling as is (`:393`), and `resolveCubeFieldName` hands it to `engine.aggregate`'s `groupBy`. This door would refuse such an entry ("'<cube>' is not a relation field"). On SQL, that qualified column may answer today, because the table is the one in FROM. Measure one query on main and on this head, over a real engine and SqlDriver/SQLite: `dimensions: ['<cube>.<field>']` where the cube does not declare `<field>` as a dimension (or the dimension gate admits it).
- If it is refused before the engine, or the qualifier is stripped, write that reading in the PR and R2 closes.
- If it reaches the door dotted and answered on main, the door must accept the object's own name as a qualifier, or the strategy must strip it. That push needs a fresh L1.

**Routing.** L2 is owed for the narrowing declaration after R1, TIER_DEFAULT by seat 5. data-1 lands after the L2. A push that only applies R1 and records R2's reading needs no fresh L1.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `874d01cae499de151b1d58c4993048873639bc7a`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/objectql/src/aggregate-query-shape-door.ts, packages/runtime/src/mcp-aggregate-relation-path-group-by.test.ts + read in the cited code at `main` `895dd437f4`, never reviewed: packages/objectql/src/engine-delete-and-aggregate.ts, packages/objectql/src/relation-group-join.ts, packages/objectql/src/group-by-structured-json-door.ts, packages/objectql/src/in-memory-aggregation.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-query-validation.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts, packages/spec/src/data/query.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/field-value.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/filter-dotted-head.ts, packages/spec/src/ui/view-grouping-query.ts, packages/drivers/driver-memory/src/memory-driver.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-aggregation.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts, packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/strategies/objectql-strategy.ts, packages/types/src/error-leak.ts, packages/types/src/data-error-classification.ts

Net diff read against merge-base `a1b14cdff8` (3 files, +200/-2). `main` has moved 24 commits since; none touches the door, and its two edits to the cited files (`engine-delete-and-aggregate.ts` in `delete`, `protocol-query-validation.ts` in the expand and filter gates) are outside the aggregate path.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set of `engine.aggregate`, narrowed — right in direction.** A `groupBy` entry (a name, or the `field` of the object form, a date bucket included) whose name contains a dot and is not a declared field is refused before any driver (`aggregate-query-shape-door.ts:214-227`). A dotted name the object does declare still falls through to the virtual-field arm (`:228`). The set refused is every dotted undeclared name, which is wider than the relation paths the PR declares and pins: see S1.
- **Refusal envelope — right, no new vocabulary.** `INVALID_FIELD` / 400 with `httpStatus`, `field`, `fields`, `object`, `param: 'groupBy'` and `path`, the shape the two sibling arms of the same function already give. The code is the one the REST door (`protocol-query-validation.ts:1111`) and the driver's missing-column backstop give for the same condition, so one condition keeps one code on three layers.
- **Position — right.** `groupBy.N` for a name, `groupBy.N.field` for the object form. A bucket over a dotted field is placed at `.field`, not `.dateGranularity`: the field is what is wrong.
- **Order among the doors — right.** The arm sits in the existing walk at `engine-delete-and-aggregate.ts:1049`, after the internal-field, credential, structured-JSON, field-type and record-currency doors, so each of those keeps its own words; inside the walk the first offending entry by index answers, dotted or virtual.
- **Observable change at the MCP tool — right.** On the bridge (`domains/mcp.ts:1277`, `:1304`, both through `callData`) a relation path moves from the driver's answer (a 400 with no `path` after the statement ran, or `DATABASE_ERROR` / 500) to one 400 before the statement. REST callers still meet the REST door first, in its words.
- **Public surface — unchanged.** No export is added (`relationPathGroupMessage` is module-private). The new import, `REFERENCE_VALUE_TYPES`, is an existing `@objectstack/spec/data` export. No spec, docs or skills file is in the diff.
- **Not judged by the arm, as before:** a registry-less host or a schema with no field map (`:205-206`), and an alias that contains a dot.

### ② Semver level

- One changeset, `@objectstack/objectql` at `patch`. The diff publishes from that package alone: the `packages/runtime` path is a test file. `Metadata-protocol: none` holds, since no key, value or metadata type an author writes moves.
- The declaration `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` (PR body and changeset, line-initial in both) is right: nothing in the diff widens an accept set or the public surface, and a runtime input that used to reach the driver is now refused.
- `patch` with the **BREAKING** banner and one ADR-0087 marker (`not-required`, `no-migration-prescription`) is the level AGENTS.md's Post-Task Checklist step 3 gives a non-protocol breaking change. Both `Check Changeset` runs on this head concluded `success`.
- The BREAKING paragraph does not cover the whole refused set: S1, item 3.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev flags, newest `os-dev-report` (card comment 7009795991), each answered.** ADR-0087 disposition in words in the PR body and as the marker in the changeset: accepted, the gate reads the changeset. Main's door restored into the tree for the R2 reading, then restored from HEAD: no residue, the diff is the three declared files. The R2 probe's composition limit and its two queue time-outs: no bearing on the contract. Read in the cited code, R2 agrees with `objectql-strategy.ts`: the strategy hands the engine resolved member names, or the relation field for a cross-object dimension, never a dotted name. Not re-measured here.
- **Round-0 flags.** The claim's `packages/plugins/driver-sql` path does not exist; the driver is at `packages/drivers/driver-sql` and is untouched. `engine-delete-and-aggregate.ts`, excluded by the claim, is untouched. The test sits in `packages/runtime`, the one package holding the bridge, the engine and `SqlDriver` together: accepted.
- **`open_questions`.** The newest report lists none. Round 0's one question (the form of the maintainer brief) was answered B by the coordinator, and the PR body carries that form.
- **SQL push-down.** No finding: the diff adds no read, no id materialisation and no in-app join. It removes a statement.
- **Author.** The PR's `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`.
- **PostgreSQL.** The dev marks that cell NOT MEASURED, and the door's header states its reading as SQLite. The door answers before any driver, so the cell does not bear on the new answer.
- **Landing prerequisites, as read at 13:00Z.**
  - Battery: comment 7009795991 is the newest `os-dev-report` on #34886 and pins the dogfood battery at this head (its `head` and `dogfood_battery` fields both carry the full sha above; verify lock `VERDICT command-exit 0`, 482 files passed, 0 failures). That is the dev's reading, not a check-run: the `Dogfood Regression Gate` shard matrix is `skipped` on this head and runs in the merge queue.
  - Check-runs: 57 on this head, all `completed`: 39 `success`, 18 `skipped`, none failed, none pending.
  - Owed before ACCEPT, on the PR body: the body carries the `(narrowing)` arm and no `Skills-docs:` line, which `l1-review-checklist.md` (范围与 changeset) makes a REWORK. A body edit, so the head does not move.
  - The PR is a draft.
  - S1 is open on this head; its fix moves the head and earns a delta review.

### ④ Design judgment

**The narrowing against the published spec on `main`: it makes the spec's own refusal real, and takes no declared capability away.**

- The spec declares a group target as a bare field name (`query.zod.ts:203`). The list-view lowering states a lookup group key is the stored id, never the related record (`view-grouping-query.ts:46`). The REST door's contract says names are judged exactly, because the aggregation contract groups by the object's own columns (`protocol.ts:5022`). `relation-group-join.ts:17` says in so many words that a dotted `groupBy` entry is still refused at its door. The `aggregate_records` description promises "Grouping fields". No skill or docs page teaches a dotted `groupBy` (searched `skills/` and `content/docs/`).
- So grouping by a path through relations was never declared on the public `groupBy`. The engine door now holds the REST door's rule for the callers that reach the engine past it. This is not a declared-and-undelivered capability narrowed at the consumer.
- The capability that is delivered, grouping by a related record's attribute for the analytics strategy, does not pass through this arm: it rides the symbol-keyed request's own `attrs` (`relation-group-join.ts`), and the FK-expand groups by the relation field. Neither sends a dotted name.
- The card's Expected is met by its refusal arm: the 4xx names the path, its depth, the depth served, and two ways to ask instead.

**Attempts to break it.**

- A declared field whose name contains a dot is kept (own-property check before the refusal). Prototype keys as a head read as undeclared.
- The words clear the client-message leak screen (`error-leak.ts`): no dialect template and no statement prefix.
- The relation remedy and the analytics path do not collide (above).

**S1 (should-fix) — the arm refuses a class the PR neither declares, measures nor pins: a dotted name whose head is not a relation.**

- The guard is `field.includes('.')` on any undeclared name (`aggregate-query-shape-door.ts:214`). Every refusal the test pins has a `lookup` head (test lines 92-120). Nothing enters the `headIsRelation === false` branch (`:174`, `:181`).
- For that class the door states as fact, of every dotted path, that it "reached the database as a qualified column name that no table here has" and that "an engine that aggregates in memory put every row into one null group" (`:182-184`). Read in the cited code, not run, two members answered otherwise before this head:
  - a path into a structured-JSON value on driver-memory: its native aggregate reads the group key with `getValueByPath` (`memory-driver.ts:335`, `:2067`), so `address.city` over stored objects came back as one group per nested value;
  - the aggregated object's own table name as the head on driver-sql: the name goes to `builder.groupBy` as a qualified identifier (`sql-driver-aggregation.ts:138`, `:229-232`), which is a valid statement and groups by the object's own column.
- Refusing both is in the contract's direction: the REST door refuses them by the exact-name rule, and limiting the arm to relation heads would leave a deep non-relation path on the 500 the card is about. The reach should stay. What is missing is that the narrowing says so. The filter axis shows why it has to be said: `filter-dotted-head.ts:33-39` deliberately leaves a path into a nested stored value unjudged, because refusing it would delete a working behaviour on two backends.
- To close S1:
  1. a pin that enters the non-relation arm: a declared non-relation head and an undeclared head, each asserting the envelope and that no statement ran;
  2. words that are true for that arm: drop the history sentence there, or say only what holds;
  3. the changeset's BREAKING paragraph naming the whole refused set (any dotted name the object does not declare), with the two shapes above either measured and stated, or not claimed as a null group.

**Nits.**

- N1 (nit) — `headIsRelation` reads the declared type alone (`:220-221`). A `lookup` or `user` field with `multiple: true` is told to group by the relation field itself, which the multi-value door refuses (`group-by-structured-json-door.ts:132`). The second refusal is clear, so the caller recovers in two steps. Fold into S1's code change, or leave as an accepted deviation.
- N2 (nit) — for the card's own path the words through the second alternative come to 459 characters, against the 500 a truncating 4xx face keeps (`data-error-classification.ts:54`). A longer object name pushes "or aggregate the related object" past the bound; the first alternative stays inside. Which faces truncate this message was not traced: REST callers meet the REST door first.
- N3 (nit) — in the test, the `aggregateGroups` case does not assert `path`, and the cases titled "no statement reaches the database" assert no `GROUP BY` statement, not no statement.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-34886-deep-groupby-refusal`
Reviewed-by: `session_01Utp6CbUb7TcZK1XUAddUmQ` (L2 subagent)

**VERDICT: PASS**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `13a5b397db366d5a394458464d61b97c80babb08`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/objectql/src/aggregate-query-shape-door.ts, packages/runtime/src/mcp-aggregate-relation-path-group-by.test.ts + read in the cited code at `main` `b65488a8a9`, never reviewed: packages/objectql/src/engine-delete-and-aggregate.ts, packages/objectql/src/group-by-structured-json-door.ts, packages/spec/src/data/field-value.zod.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-query-validation.ts, packages/drivers/driver-memory/src/memory-driver.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-aggregation.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts, packages/types/src/error-leak.ts, scripts/pm/label-write.mjs

Delta review of record 7010069867 (head `874d01cae4`, PASS with S1). Read: the two fix commits `ce0a9509e5` and `e8b311e4c0`, the merge `13a5b397db`, the net diff against `main` (3 files, +242/-2), card comment 7013990082, and the check-runs on this head and on `e8b311e4c0`.

S1: closed

N1, N2 and N3 are taken as well; one new nit, N4, is in ④.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set — unchanged since the reviewed head, right.** The guard is the same line (`aggregate-query-shape-door.ts:231`), and so are the envelope, the position and the call site. The fix round moved words, docblocks and one import (`isMultiValueField`, an existing `@objectstack/spec/data` export).
- **Refusal words — now chosen by the head, right.** `DottedHead` (`:176`) reads the head's declaration three ways (`:238-240`): a single-valued relation, a multi-value relation, anything else. Only a relation head is counted in hops (`:194-198`). A head that is no relation gets one sentence that holds for all its members: the dotted name is not a field of the object, name the field without a qualifier, or store the part in a field of its own (`:189-193`). No sentence about what a backend or an in-memory engine did remains in any refusal.
- **Nothing else moved.** `874d01cae4..e8b311e4c0` touches the three PR paths and nothing else. `e8b311e4c0..13a5b397db` is the merge alone, and the three paths are byte-identical across it.

### ② Semver level

- Unchanged: `@objectstack/objectql` at `patch`, the declaration `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` with `Metadata-protocol: none` in the PR body and the changeset, the **BREAKING** banner, one ADR-0087 marker.
- The BREAKING paragraph now names the whole refused set, any dotted entry that is not itself a field, in three shapes, with what each answered before. The relation path keeps its null-group reading in memory. The JSON sub-path is stated as the driver's own 400 on SQLite and as groups by the nested value in memory. The own-name qualifier is stated as an answer under 200 grouped by the bare column. Neither of the last two is claimed as a null group. The SQLite readings of both are measured (the round's ablation: the JSON pin met the driver backstop, the own-name pin was answered); the in-memory JSON reading is a code read, and it agrees with mine (`memory-driver.ts:2067`).
- `Check Changeset` concluded `success` on this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev flags, newest `os-dev-report` (card comment 7013990082), each answered.**
  - A commit trailer that named a model was amended before it was published: no contract bearing, nothing published was rewritten.
  - The merge-base door restored into the worktree for the scenarios base leg, then restored from HEAD: no residue, the diff is the three declared files.
  - The dev's note that record 7010069867 read the battery at `874d01cae4`: correct. That record reviewed `874d01cae4` and read the battery pinned there; the battery at `e8b311e4c0` is the one in 7013990082.
  - The four-line maintainer brief still describes relation paths only, with the wider set in the BREAKING line: the seat's wording, accepted here. The brief's worst case (a caller that relied on the grouping is now refused) covers all three shapes.
- **`open_questions`.** None.
- **`out_of_scope_findings`.** The scenarios timeout, noted and not filed by the dev: answered below under the check-runs, and already fixed on `main` by #35531.
- **`Skills-docs:`.** The PR body now carries `Skills-docs: none` with its reason, which agrees with round 1's search: no skill or docs page teaches a dotted `groupBy` entry.
- **SQL push-down.** No finding: the fix round adds no read.
- **The merge.** `13a5b397db` has two parents, `e8b311e4c0` and `b65488a8a9`, which is `main`'s tip. It brings 44 commits. Its tree is the tree git computes for that merge (`git merge-tree --write-tree` of the two parents gives `11662b5174`, the head's tree), so nothing was resolved by hand. On the `main` side, none of the 44 commits touches a PR path, the door's call site, the aggregate body of `engine-delete-and-aggregate.ts` (its three hunks are in `delete`), `field-value.zod.ts`, `domains/mcp.ts` or `sql-driver-aggregation.ts`.
